$comment: INTENDED lifecycle rules for the B2 archive bucket. See
scripts/apply-bucket-lifecycle.mjs for why this is committed and how to
apply or verify it. Changing a number here is a reviewable change;
changing it in the Backblaze console is not, which is the whole point.
EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS BOUNDED BY A PUBLISHED PROMISE, NOT BY TASTE.
The ceilings, why the worst case is the SUM of both terms, why the daily
ceiling is 29 rather than 30, and why the recovery term has a floor are all
documented once in scripts/lifecycle-policy.mjs, which BOTH writers
(apply-bucket-lifecycle.mjs and setup-backblaze.mjs) must pass through.
Reasoning is not duplicated here, because a second copy is a second thing
to go stale — which is exactly what happened to the 30/60-day explanation
this file used to carry in three places.
Daily (archives/, manifests/): 20 + 9 = 29 days worst case.
- 29 not 30: PrivacyPolicy.md promises a ticket's backup copies persist at
most 30 days beyond deletion, the B2 clock starts at UPLOAD, and a ticket
can be pruned from D1 between export and upload. A day of headroom.
- 9 not 7: the forged-overwrite detector is the WEEKLY healthcheck, so at 7
the alert races the deletion. 9 puts detection strictly inside the window
and leaves two days to act.
Monthly (archives-monthly/, manifests-monthly/): 356 + 9 = 365 days.
- PrivacyPolicy.md and the rendered privacy page both promise monthly
archives are kept 12 months and then age out. The previous 365 + 30 came
to 395 and overshot that by a month.
- The same 9-day recovery term, for the same reason.
Raising the daily ceiling at all means excluding support_tickets from the
daily tier, which means tickets have no backup — a product decision, #1474.
